questions.question: Who was the constitutional advisor to the Constituent Assembly?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**B.N. Rau**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sir Benegal Narsing Rau** was appointed as the **Constitutional Advisor** to the **Constituent Assembly** in **1946** to assist in the democratic transition and legal structuring of independent India.
 
• He was responsible for preparing the **initial draft** of the **Constitution of India** in **October 1947**, which originally contained **243 articles** and **13 schedules**.
 
• To formulate the framework, **B.N. Rau** traveled to the **USA**, **Canada**, **Ireland**, and the **United Kingdom** to consult with constitutional experts and jurists, including **Justice Felix Frankfurter** of the US Supreme Court.
 
• The **Drafting Committee**, led by **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**, utilized **B.N. Rau’s** preliminary draft as the base document to refine and finalize the ultimate text of the Constitution.
 
• Beyond his work in India, he was an eminent jurist who also assisted in drafting the **Constitution of Burma** (Myanmar) in **1947** and served as a judge at the **International Court of Justice** in **The Hague**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar**:

 
 
• An eminent lawyer and former **Advocate General** of the Madras State.
 
• He served as a key member of the **Drafting Committee** and played a vital role in shaping the provisions related to **Fundamental Rights**.
 
 
 
• **T.T. Krishnamachari**:
 
 
• A prominent businessman and politician who was inducted into the **Drafting Committee** in **1948**.
 
• He filled the vacancy created after the death of **D.P. Khaitan** and later served as the **Union Finance Minister** of India.
 
 
 
• **K.M. Munshi**:
 
 
• **Kanaiyalal Maneklal Munshi** was a lawyer and independence activist who was a member of the **Drafting Committee**.
 
• He is also known for founding the **Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan** in **1938** to promote Indian culture and education.

questions.question: Santhal Dance is predominantly performed during which occasion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harvest festivals and religious ceremonies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Santhal dance** is a vibrant and ancient folk dance performed by the **Santhal tribe**, which is one of the largest **Scheduled Tribes** in India, primarily settled in **Jharkhand**, **West Bengal**, **Odisha**, and **Bihar**.
 
• This traditional dance is deeply connected to the agrarian lifestyle of the community and is predominantly performed during **harvest festivals** to express gratitude to the gods and nature for a successful yield.
 
• The most significant occasion for this dance is the **Sohrai festival**, celebrated in the month of **October or November** (after the Kharif harvest), where men and women dance together to the rhythmic beats of traditional drums.
 
• It is also performed during **religious ceremonies** such as **Baha** (the flower festival), which marks the spring season and the arrival of the **Sal** blossoms, honoring the supreme deity **Marang Buru**.
 
• The dance movements are characterized by synchronized steps where dancers form **semi-circles** or **lines**, often holding hands or waist-to-waist, symbolizing **communal harmony** and social cohesion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Santhal Musical Instruments**:

 
 
• **Madal**: A traditional two-headed drum made of clay or wood, which serves as the primary rhythmic heartbeat of the dance.
 
• **Tiriao**: A bamboo flute used to provide melodic accompaniment to the percussion.
 
• **Dhamsa**: A large kettle drum used to add depth and intensity to the performance.
 
 
 
• **Santhal Tribe Heritage**:
 
 
• They follow the **Sarna religion**, which is based on the worship of **nature spirits** and sacred groves known as **Jaher**.
 
• Their language, **Santhali**, is written in the **Ol Chiki** script, which was developed by **Pandit Raghunath Murmu** in 1925.
 
 
 
• **Other Festivals**:
 
 
• **Karam Festival**: Observed to seek blessings for the protection of crops and the well-being of the family.
 
• **Erok-Sim**: A ritual ceremony performed during the sowing of seeds at the start of the monsoon.

questions.question: Tippani dance is traditionally performed during which occasions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Weddings and festivals**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tippani dance** is a prominent folk dance originating from the **Saurashtra** region of **Gujarat**, particularly associated with the coastal towns of **Chorwad** and **Veraval**.
 
• The dance is traditionally performed by the women of the **Koli** and **Bhil** communities, who originally developed these rhythmic movements while working as laborers to level the ground during the construction of houses and forts.
 
• While it has its roots in manual labor, the performance has evolved into a celebratory art form conducted during significant social and cultural events, such as **weddings** and major **Hindu festivals** like **Holi** and **Diwali**.
 
• The performance is characterized by the use of the **Tippani stick**, a long wooden pole roughly **175 cm** in length with a heavy square wooden or iron block (called a **Garbo**) attached at the base to strike the floor.
 
• The dancers arrange themselves in two rows and strike the floor in a synchronized, rhythmic pattern, creating a unique sound that serves as both music and a display of physical coordination and endurance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Instruments and Music**:

 
 
• The rhythmic thumping of the **Tippani** is accompanied by folk instruments like the **Zanz**, **Manjira** (cymbals), **Tabla**, and **Dhol** (drum) to maintain a steady tempo.
 
• The **Turi** and **Shehnai** are also frequently used to provide melodic accompaniment to the percussive nature of the dance.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Context**:
 
 
• Unlike purely **Religious rituals** that are confined to temples, Tippani is a social dance that brings the community together in public squares or household courtyards.
 
• The costumes worn are traditional Gujarati attire, including the **Ghagra-Choli** for women, often embellished with mirrors and vibrant embroidery typical of the **Saurashtra** folk style.
 
• It is often compared to other work-related folk dances, but it stands out due to its high energy and the **percussive floor-striking** technique which is rare in other Indian folk traditions.

questions.question: The Satpura Range is located in which part of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Central India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Satpura Range** is a major mountain system located in **Central India**, forming a significant part of the Indian peninsula's geographic backbone.
 
• Geographically, it extends in an **east-west direction** across the states of **Gujarat**, **Maharashtra**, **Madhya Pradesh**, and **Chhattisgarh**.
 
• The range is situated between two major west-flowing rivers: the **Narmada River** to the north and the **Tapti River** to the south.
 
• It runs parallel to the **Vindhya Range**, and together they create a natural divide between the **Indo-Gangetic Plain** of Northern India and the **Deccan Plateau** of the south.
 
• The name 'Satpura' is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Sapta' (seven) and 'Pura' (mountains), signifying the **seven folds** or hills that constitute the range.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geological Characteristics:**

 
 
• The Satpura Range is classified as a **block mountain** (horst), formed due to tectonic activity that created **rift valleys** (graben) on either side.
 
• The range is composed primarily of **basaltic rocks** in the west, while its eastern sections are made of **Gondwana formations** and metamorphic rocks.
 
 
 
• **Highest Peak and Sub-ranges:**
 
 
• **Dhupgarh**, located in the **Mahadeo Hills** near the hill station of Pachmarhi, is the highest peak of the Satpura Range, standing at **1,350 meters**.
 
• The range includes several distinct hilly tracts such as the **Rajpipla Hills**, **Gawilgarh Hills**, and the **Maikal Range**.
 
 
 
• **River Systems and Biodiversity:**
 
 
• The **Amarkantak Plateau**, where the Satpura and Vindhya ranges meet, is the source of the **Narmada** and **Son** rivers.
 
• The range is home to rich deciduous forests and famous tiger reserves, including **Kanha National Park**, **Satpura National Park**, and **Pench National Park**.

questions.question: Which Indian leader served as the president of India from 1992 to 1997 and had a distinguished academic background in constitutional law?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shankar Dayal Sharma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shankar Dayal Sharma** served as the **9th President of India** from **25 July 1992 to 25 July 1997**.
 
• He was a distinguished legal luminary who obtained his **PhD** from **Fitzwilliam College, Cambridge University**, and was a member of **Lincoln's Inn**.
 
• His academic excellence included teaching law at the **University of Cambridge** and **Lucknow University**, and he was also a **Fellow at Harvard Law School**.
 
• Prior to his presidency, he served as the **8th Vice President of India** (1987−1992) and as the **Union Minister for Communications** (1974−1977).
 
• He had a prolific political career, serving as the **Chief Minister of Bhopal State** (1952−1956) and the **President of the Indian National Congress** (1972−1974).
 
• During his five-year presidential term, he navigated a period of political transition by swearing in **four different Prime Ministers**: P. V. Narasimha Rao, Atal Bihari Vajpayee, H. D. Deve Gowda, and I. K. Gujral.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ramaswamy Venkataraman**

 
 
• He served as the **8th President of India** from **1987 to 1992**.
 
• He was a lawyer and independence activist who previously held the portfolios of **Finance Minister** and **Defence Minister**.
 
 
 
• **K. R. Narayanan**
 
 
• He served as the **10th President of India** from **1997 to 2002**.
 
• He was the first member of the **Dalit community** to hold the office and had a distinguished career as a **diplomat** and **Ambassador**.
 
 
 
• **Giani Zail Singh**
 
 
• He served as the **7th President of India** from **1982 to 1987**.
 
• He was the first **Sikh President** and previously served as the **Chief Minister of Punjab** and the **Union Home Minister**.

questions.question: The Human Development Index (HDI) is a composite index of

options.text: Gross Domestic Product, Gross National Income, Literacy

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Education, Income, Life expectancy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Human Development Index (HDI)** is a composite statistical tool used to measure a country's overall achievement in its social and economic dimensions, shifting the focus from purely economic growth to human-centric development.
 
• It was created by Pakistani economist **Mahbub ul Haq** and Indian Nobel laureate **Amartya Sen** and has been published annually by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** since **1990**.
 
• The index is calculated using three basic dimensions: a **Long and healthy life**, **Knowledge**, and a **Decent standard of living**.
 
• The **Health** dimension is assessed by **Life expectancy at birth**, which serves as a proxy for the quality of a nation's healthcare system, nutrition, and environmental safety.
 
• The **Knowledge** or **Education** dimension is measured through a combination of the **Mean years of schooling** for adults aged 25 years and older and the **Expected years of schooling** for children of school-entering age.
 
• The **Standard of Living** is quantified using **Gross National Income (GNI) per capita** adjusted for **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)** in US dollars to account for differences in the cost of living across countries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Methodology and Scoring**:

 
 
• HDI values range between **0 and 1**; a score closer to 1 indicates a higher level of human development.
 
• Countries are categorized into four tiers: **Very High** (0.800 and above), **High** (0.700–0.799), **Medium** (0.550–0.699), and **Low Human Development** (below 0.550).
 
• The final index is the **geometric mean** of the normalized indices for each of the three dimensions, ensuring that poor performance in one area is not masked by high performance in another.
 
 
 
• **Extended Indices**:
 
 
• To address criticisms of the HDI, the UNDP introduced the **Inequality-adjusted HDI (IHDI)** in 2010 to account for how achievements are distributed among the population.
 
• Other related metrics include the **Gender Inequality Index (GII)**, which measures gender-based disadvantages, and the **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)**, which identifies overlapping deprivations.
 
• While **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** measures economic output, HDI is considered a more holistic indicator as it incorporates social indicators like **literacy** and **longevity**.

questions.question: The tilt of Earth's axis varies between 22.1° and 24.5° over 41,000 years (Milankovitch cycles). How does this variation affect Earth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Greater tilt increases seasonal contrast**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Axial tilt**, also known as **obliquity**, is the angle between Earth's rotational axis and its orbital plane, currently measuring approximately **23.5 degrees**.
 
• The tilt fluctuates between **22.1 degrees** and **24.5 degrees** over a cycle of roughly **41,000 years**, a phenomenon identified by Serbian scientist **Milutin Milankovitch**.
 
• When the tilt is at its maximum (**24.5 degrees**), each hemisphere receives more direct **solar radiation** during its summer and significantly less during its winter, which **increases seasonal contrast**.
 
• A greater tilt results in hotter summers and colder winters because the higher latitudes are oriented more directly toward or away from the **Sun** during solstices.
 
• Conversely, a minimum tilt of **22.1 degrees** leads to milder seasons; cooler summers in this phase often prevent winter snow from melting entirely, facilitating the growth of **ice sheets** and triggering **glaciation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Milankovitch Cycles** include two other primary variations:

 
 
• **Eccentricity**: This refers to the shape of Earth's orbit around the Sun, which shifts from nearly circular to mildly elliptical over **100,000-year** and **400,000-year** cycles, affecting the total **insolation** received.
 
• **Precession**: Often called the Earth's 'wobble', this **26,000-year cycle** changes the orientation of the axis, determining which hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun at **perihelion** (closest approach) or **aphelion** (farthest point).
 
 
 
• **Orbital Speed**: The speed at which Earth travels is governed by **Kepler's Second Law** and is influenced by **eccentricity** (distance from the Sun), not the tilt of the axis.
 
• **Magnetic Field**: Earth's magnetism is generated by the **geodynamo** effect in the **outer core** and is independent of the orbital **obliquity** cycles.

questions.question: What is the primary architectural style of the French Quarter in Pondicherry?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indo-French Colonial**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **French Quarter** of **Puducherry**, historically known as **Ville Blanche** (White Town), is globally recognized for its **Indo-French Colonial** architecture, a unique blend of 18th-century **European designs** and **local Indian** structural adaptations.
 
• The area is characterized by a **Cartesian grid** street layout, a common feature of **French urban planning**, where streets intersect at right angles, providing an organized and airy atmosphere.
 
• Buildings typically feature **high compound walls** and **monumental arched gateways** that lead into **private courtyards**, which were designed to provide privacy and natural cooling in a **tropical climate**.
 
• The aesthetic is defined by **lime-plastered walls** painted in a palette of **yellow ochre**, **mustard**, and **white**, which reflect the sunlight and help maintain a cooler internal temperature.
 
• Architectural details include **tall windows** with **wooden louvered shutters** (persiennes), **wide verandahs**, and **ornamental cornices**, showcasing a synthesis of **French elegance** and **practical regional design**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gothic Revival**:

 
 
• While not the primary style of the quarter, it is seen in religious landmarks like the **Basilica of the Sacred Heart of Jesus**, featuring **pointed arches** and **stained glass**.
 
 
 
• **Neoclassical Style**:
 
 
• This style influenced many **institutional buildings** in Pondicherry, such as **Raj Nivas** and the **Old Court Building**, characterized by **columns**, **pediments**, and **symmetrical facades**.
 
 
 
• **Tamil Quarter (Ville Noire)**:
 
 
• Located across the **Canal**, this area features **vernacular Tamil architecture** with **Thinnais** (raised street porches) and **carved wooden pillars**, which occasionally adopted **French decorative motifs** over time.
 
 
 
• **Preservation**:
 
 
• The **INTACH** (Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage) has played a significant role in restoring these **colonial heritage buildings** to maintain the city's historical identity.

questions.question: Orion is a ______ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**constellation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Orion** is one of the most prominent and recognizable **constellations** in the night sky, characterized by its location on the **celestial equator**, which makes it visible globally.
 
• Named after a giant hunter in **Greek mythology**, it is commonly referred to as **The Hunter** and is listed as one of the 88 modern constellations defined by the **International Astronomical Union** (IAU).
 
• The constellation is most easily identified by **Orion's Belt**, an asterism formed by three bright stars: **Alnitak**, **Alnilam**, and **Mintaka**.
 
• It contains two of the ten brightest stars in the sky: **Rigel** (a blue supergiant) and **Betelgeuse** (a red supergiant).
 
• It also houses the **Orion Nebula** (M42), a massive region of dust and gas where new stars are being born, visible even to the naked eye as a fuzzy patch.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Star**:

 
 
• A massive, luminous ball of **plasma** held together by **gravity**, undergoing **nuclear fusion** in its core. While Orion *contains* stars like **Saiph** and **Bellatrix**, the name Orion refers to the entire group.
 
 
 
• **Planet**:
 
 
• A celestial body that orbits a star, has sufficient mass for its self-gravity to make it **spherical**, and has **cleared its neighborhood** of other objects, such as **Venus** or **Jupiter**.
 
 
 
• **Satellite**:
 
 
• An object that orbits a planet or another body larger than itself. This includes **natural satellites** like the **Moon** and **artificial satellites** launched for **telecommunications** or research.

questions.question: Who is considered the first official World Chess Champion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wilhelm Steinitz**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Wilhelm Steinitz**, an Austrian-American chess master, is recognized as the **first official World Chess Champion**.
 
• He earned this title in **1886** after defeating **Johannes Zukertort** in a match specifically organized to determine the world champion.
 
• The match took place between **January and April 1886** across three major American cities: **New York**, **St. Louis**, and **New Orleans**.
 
• Steinitz held the title for eight consecutive years until **1894**, when he was eventually defeated by **Emanuel Lasker**.
 
• He is often called the **father of modern chess** because he developed the **positional theory**, which replaced the aggressive **Romantic style** of play with a more strategic, defensive approach based on pawn structures and small advantages.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bobby Fischer**:

 
 
• An American Grandmaster who became the **11th World Chess Champion** in **1972**.
 
• He defeated **Boris Spassky** in a historic match in **Reykjavik**, ending decades of Soviet chess dominance.
 
 
 
• **Garry Kasparov**:
 
 
• A Russian legend who became the **13th World Chess Champion** in **1985** at the age of 22.
 
• He is widely considered one of the greatest players in history and held the world number one ranking for a record-breaking **255 months**.
 
 
 
• **Paul Morphy**:
 
 
• A 19th-century American chess prodigy who was the strongest player of the **1850s**.
 
• While he defeated every major opponent of his era, he is regarded as an **unofficial world champion** because the official title had not yet been established.

questions.question: Which type of action is heartbeat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Involuntary action**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Involuntary actions** are biological processes or movements that occur without the conscious control or will of an individual.
 
• The **heartbeat** is classified as an involuntary action because it is performed automatically by the body to ensure continuous **blood circulation**, requiring no deliberate thought.
 
• These functions are primarily regulated by the **Autonomic Nervous System (ANS)**, which manages internal organ operations.
 
• The **Medulla Oblongata**, situated in the **hindbrain**, acts as the primary control center for regulating the **heart rate**, **breathing**, and **blood pressure**.
 
• The rhythmic contraction of the heart is initiated by the **Sinoatrial (SA) node**, often referred to as the **natural pacemaker**, located in the right atrium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reflex Action**

 
 
• This is a rapid, spontaneous response to a stimulus, such as the **knee-jerk reflex** or **blinking** of eyes.
 
• It is usually controlled by the **spinal cord** to protect the body from immediate harm.
 
 
 
• **Voluntary Action**
 
 
• These actions are under the direct control of the **cerebrum** and involve conscious decision-making.
 
• Examples include **writing**, **cycling**, and **dancing**.
 
 
 
• **Cardiac Muscles**
 
 
• The heart is composed of unique **striated muscles** that are **myogenic** in nature, meaning they can initiate contraction without external nerve impulses.
 
• These muscles never fatigue, allowing the heart to beat approximately **72 times per minute** throughout a person's lifetime.

questions.question: Which of the following is the primary function of lysosomes in a cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Waste disposal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lysosomes** are membrane-bound vesicular structures formed by the process of packaging in the **Golgi apparatus**.
 
• They serve as the **waste disposal system** of the cell by digesting foreign materials, such as bacteria and food, as well as **worn-out cell organelles**.
 
• These organelles contain a variety of **hydrolytic enzymes** (including lipases, proteases, and carbohydrases) that are capable of breaking down all major classes of biological macromolecules.
 
• The enzymes within a lysosome are optimally active at an **acidic pH** (approximately 4.5 to 5.0), which is maintained by **proton pumps** in the lysosomal membrane.
 
• In the event of cellular damage or malfunction, lysosomes may burst, leading to the **autolysis** or self-digestion of the cell; for this reason, they are famously known as the **suicide bags** of the cell.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Energy production**:

 
 
• This is the primary role of the **mitochondria**, often referred to as the **powerhouse of the cell**.
 
• Mitochondria produce **ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate)** through the process of **oxidative phosphorylation** during cellular respiration.
 
 
 
• **Protein synthesis**:
 
 
• This process is carried out by **ribosomes**, which can be found floating freely in the **cytoplasm** or attached to the **Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER)**.
 
• The **nucleolus** within the nucleus is responsible for the synthesis of ribosomal RNA (rRNA).
 
 
 
• **Storage of lipids**:
 
 
• The **Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER)** is the major site for the **synthesis and storage of lipids** and steroid hormones.
 
• In specialized animal cells, lipids are stored in large quantities within **adipocytes** (fat cells) in the form of **triglycerides**.

questions.question: Which is the largest saltwater lake in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chilika Lake**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chilika Lake**, located in the state of **Odisha** on the eastern coast of India, is the **largest brackish water lagoon** in India and the **second largest** in the world.
 
• It spreads across the **Puri, Khurda,** and **Ganjam** districts at the mouth of the **Daya River**, covering an area that fluctuates between **900 and 1,165 square kilometers** during different seasons.
 
• In **1981**, it was designated as the **first Indian wetland** of international importance under the **Ramsar Convention** due to its rich biodiversity.
 
• The lake serves as a massive wintering ground for **migratory birds** traveling from the **Caspian Sea, Lake Baikal, Aral Sea,** and other remote regions of **Central and South-East Asia**.
 
• It is one of the few places in the world where the endangered **Irrawaddy Dolphins** can be spotted, particularly near the **Satapada** island area.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vembanad Lake**:

 
 
• Located in **Kerala**, it is recognized as the **longest lake** in India.
 
• It is the venue for the famous **Nehru Trophy Boat Race** and is a major hub for **backwater tourism**.
 
 
 
• **Pulicat Lake**:
 
 
• Straddling the border of **Andhra Pradesh** and **Tamil Nadu**, it is the **second largest** brackish water lake in India.
 
• The **Satish Dhawan Space Centre** is situated on the **Sriharikota Island**, which separates this lake from the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
 
 
• **Sambhar Lake**:
 
 
• Situated in **Rajasthan** near Jaipur, it is India's **largest inland saltwater lake**.
 
• It is a significant source of **salt production** and a designated **Ramsar site**, known for attracting large populations of **flamingos**.

questions.question: In November 2024, which country has become the first country to pass a law banning social media use for children under the age of 16?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Australia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **November 2024**, the **Australian Parliament** officially passed a historic and world-first law that prohibits children under the age of **16** from using **social media platforms**.
 
• The legislation, titled the **Online Safety Amendment (Social Media Minimum Age) Bill 2024**, aims to mitigate the negative impacts of digital platforms on the **mental health** and **physical safety** of young people.
 
• Under this law, the burden of enforcement lies entirely with the **social media companies** (such as **Meta**, **TikTok**, **X**, and **Snapchat**) rather than the parents or the children themselves.
 
• The law does not provide any exemptions for **parental consent**, making it one of the most stringent digital regulations globally.
 
• Companies that fail to demonstrate **systemic compliance** in preventing underage access can face massive financial penalties of up to **50 million Australian dollars** (approximately $32.5 million USD).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Implementation Details:
 
 
• The law includes a **12-month grace period** for tech platforms to develop and implement robust **age-verification mechanisms** before enforcement begins.
 
• The **eSafety Commissioner** of **Australia** will oversee the regulatory framework and provide guidance to platforms on meeting the required standards of **online safety**.
 
 
 
• Exemptions and Scope:
 
 
• Certain services, including **YouTube**, **WhatsApp**, and educational platforms, are expected to be exempt to ensure continued access to **educational content** and **private messaging**.
 
• The policy focuses on platforms characterized by **algorithmic feeds** and social networking features that are deemed most addictive or harmful to minors.

questions.question: In which year did the First Anglo-Mysore war take place?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1767-69**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **First Anglo-Mysore War** was a major military conflict in India that took place between **1767 and 1769**.
 
• It was fought between the **Kingdom of Mysore**, under the leadership of **Hyder Ali**, and the **British East India Company**.
 
• The war was preceded by a **tripartite alliance** formed in **1766** involving the British, the **Nizam of Hyderabad**, and the **Marathas** against Mysore.
 
• **Hyder Ali** successfully broke the alliance through strategic diplomacy, convincing the **Marathas** to withdraw and the **Nizam** to switch sides and support Mysore against the British.
 
• In a decisive move, Hyder Ali reached the outskirts of **Madras** (now Chennai), threatening the British headquarters and forcing them to negotiate.
 
• The conflict concluded with the signing of the **Treaty of Madras** on **April 4, 1769**, which was a **defensive alliance** ensuring the mutual return of conquered territories and assistance in case of a third-party attack.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The struggle for supremacy in South India continued through three more wars:
 
 
• **Second Anglo-Mysore War (1780-1784):** Sparked by the British capture of **Mahe**; it ended with the **Treaty of Mangalore** after the death of Hyder Ali.
 
• **Third Anglo-Mysore War (1790-1792):** Fought between **Tipu Sultan** and the British under **Lord Cornwallis**, resulting in the **Treaty of Seringapatam** and Mysore losing half its territory.
 
• **Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799):** Initiated by **Lord Wellesley**, this final conflict ended with the fall of **Seringapatam** and the death of **Tipu Sultan**, leading to the restoration of the **Wodeyar dynasty** under British **Subsidiary Alliance**.

questions.question: Which political party did well in the "General" constituencies during the 1946 provincial elections?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian National Congress**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **1946 Provincial Elections** were a pivotal moment in the history of **British India**, held to determine the composition of the provincial legislatures and the **Constituent Assembly**.
 
• The **Indian National Congress** secured a massive victory in the **General constituencies**, winning nearly **90.5%** of the non-Muslim votes and establishing its dominance across the majority of provinces.
 
• This landslide performance enabled the **Congress** to form ministries in eight out of the eleven provinces, including **Madras**, **Bombay**, **United Provinces**, **Bihar**, **Orissa**, and the **Central Provinces**.
 
• The election results confirmed a polarized mandate where the **Congress** represented the general electorate and the **Muslim League** secured the vast majority of the reserved **Muslim seats**.
 
• The **1946 elections** were conducted under the **Government of India Act of 1935**, which provided for a limited franchise based on property, tax, and educational qualifications, covering about **13%** of the adult population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Muslim League**:

 
 
• Under the leadership of **Muhammad Ali Jinnah**, the party won **425 out of 492** seats reserved for Muslims, effectively validating their demand for a separate state of **Pakistan**.
 
 
 
• **Communist Party of India (CPI)**:
 
 
• The **CPI** contested the 1946 elections separately from the Congress for the first time but performed poorly, managing to win only **8 seats** across all provincial assemblies.
 
 
 
• **Justice Party**:
 
 
• Based primarily in the **Madras Presidency**, this party advocated for **non-Brahmin** rights but had lost its political relevance by 1946, having been largely absorbed by the **Dravidar Kazhagam** movement.
 
 
 
• **Swaraj Party**:
 
 
• Founded in **1923** by **Motilal Nehru** and **Chittaranjan Das** to enter the legislative councils, the party had ceased to function as an independent political entity long before the 1946 elections.
